qs.q: A 10-month-old infant is brought to a clinic for routine growth assessment. Physical examination reveals thin limbs and diminished subcutaneous fat, but no bilateral pitting oedema. Anthropometry shows a weight-for-height Z-score of -3.5. What is the most accurate classification of this infant's nutritional status?
qs.e: A weight-for-height Z-score below -3 standard deviations defines severe acute malnutrition (severe wasting) even in the absence of nutritional oedema. Moderate acute malnutrition corresponds to a Z-score between -2 and -3 standard deviations.
qs.s: Paediatric Nutrition: Infant Feeding, Nutritional Assessment and: MCQs
